section_summary: This section contains correspondence and intelligence regarding American financial policy toward Japan in March and April 1938. It includes a letter and a 187-signature petition from American citizens in China protesting proposed cotton and financial loans to Japan, along with State Department instructions acknowledging the protest. In addition, the documents record reports on Japanese economic conditions, a 20,000,000 yen gold shipment from Kobe to San Francisco, the transmittal of Japan's 1937 financial annual, and internal State Department policy discussions regarding American bank credits and branch plant bond purchases in Japan.

subfiles.about: Conclusion of a letter urging President Roosevelt to deny cotton and financial loans to Japan to uphold international law and protect American interests.
subfiles.summary: Hipps concludes by arguing that loans to Japan alienate China and damage American cotton interests, urging Roosevelt to use financial leverage to end the war.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. B. Hipps to President Franklin D. Roosevelt Regarding Loans to Japan

subfiles.about: A six-page telegram transmitting the protest and names of 187 Americans residing in China against proposed cotton and other loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: This six-page telegram transmitted to President Franklin D. Roosevelt conveys a protest from 187 American citizens residing in China against cotton and other financial loans to Japan. Sent via Honolulu to avoid Japanese censorship in Shanghai, it lists the names of all 187 signatories, noting that physical signatures have been forwarded by mail.
subfiles.title: Telegram from 187 American Citizens in China to President Franklin D. Roosevelt Protesting Loans to Japan

subfiles.about: Instruction directing consular acknowledgment of J. B. Hipps's letter and telegram protesting loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State instructs the American consular officer in Shanghai to acknowledge J. B. Hipps's letter and telegram and state they received careful consideration.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Consular Officer in Charge, Shanghai
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in charge, Shanghai

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note for Tokyo despatch No. 2813 reporting on Japan's economic position and Standard-Vacuum Company meetings.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet for Tokyo despatch No. 2813 regarding Japan's economic position and Standard-Vacuum Company talks with Japanese officials.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Regarding Despatch No. 2813 on Japan's Economic and Financial Position

subfiles.about: Reporting that the Bank of Japan shipped 20,000,000 yen in gold from Kobe to San Francisco on April 13.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that the Bank of Japan notified the Commercial Attaché of a 20,000,000 yen gold shipment from Kobe to San Francisco aboard the SS Kinai Maru.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 247 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew Regarding Japanese Gold Shipment

subfiles.about: Departmental paraphrase of confidential telegram No. 247 concerning a 20,000,000 yen gold shipment from Kobe to San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Confidential paraphrase of telegram No. 247 reporting the shipment of 20,000,000 yen in gold from Kobe to San Francisco aboard the SS Kinai Maru.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 247 from the American Embassy in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmittal of copies of the paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 247 to the Secretary of the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits six copies of the paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 247 to the Secretary of the Treasury.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Note from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Transmitting two copies of the 1937 Financial and Economic Annual of Japan published by the Japanese Department of Finance.
keywords: Financial and Economic Annual of Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits two copies of the thirty-seventh Financial and Economic Annual of Japan for 1937, published in English by the Japanese Department of Finance.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2859 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew Transmitting the 1937 Financial Annual of Japan

subfiles.about: Recommending policy revisions regarding American bank credits and American branch plant investments in Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Feis suggests avoiding the term 'short term' for bank credits to Japan and candidly acknowledging that American branch plants in Japan have purchased Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Herbert Feis to Maxwell M. Hamilton Regarding Credits to Japan
